project_summary: Write and finish a first draft of an 80,000-word literary novel in 6 months while working a full-time engineering job. No outline yet, genre undecided, no prior novel completion. Target: ~440 words/day, every day.

failure_risks.risk: Sustaining ~440 publishable-draft words per day for 26 consecutive weeks alongside a full-time engineering job is a pace that almost no first-time novelist hits; the most likely failure is a stall around weeks 6-10 when the initial energy fades and the middle of the book has no map.

action_map.validation_step: Test whether the writer can sustain the required pace for 4 consecutive weeks before committing to 26.
action_map.minimum_test: Run a 4-week pilot at 440 words/day. Track actual words written daily. Use the same time slot the writer plans to use for the full run.
action_map.success_metric: ≥80% of days hit ≥440 words AND total ≥10,000 words across the 4 weeks AND no week with 3+ missed days.
action_map.failure_threshold: <60% of days hit target, OR total <7,500 words, OR 2+ weeks with 3+ missed days, OR self-reported burnout score ≥7/10 at week 4.
action_map.next_action: If pass: commit to the 6-month plan. If fail: cut scope to a 30,000-word novella, OR extend the timeline to 12 months at 200 words/day.

failure_risks.risk: Without a chosen genre, target reader, or outline, the draft will diverge stylistically and structurally; the writer will end up with 30,000-50,000 words of unrelated fragments rather than a coherent novel, and abandon the project to start over.

action_map.validation_step: Confirm that a single coherent novel exists in the writer's head before drafting.
action_map.minimum_test: Spend one weekend producing: a 1-paragraph premise, a named genre, a target reader profile, and a chapter-by-chapter outline (15-25 chapters, 1-3 sentences each).
action_map.success_metric: All four artifacts exist, the outline reaches a defined ending, and the writer can describe the protagonist's arc in 3 sentences without rereading notes.
action_map.failure_threshold: Outline stalls before the midpoint, OR the writer wants to change the premise after writing it, OR no defined ending after the weekend.
action_map.next_action: If pass: begin drafting from chapter 1. If fail: spend another 2 weekends on outline-only work, OR pivot to a short story collection where each piece is self-contained.

failure_risks.risk: Over a 6-month window, real life produces predictable disruptions (job crunch, illness, family obligations, holidays) that consume 3-6 weeks of writing time; the plan has no buffer, so any single disruption pushes the deadline past the target and motivation collapses.

action_map.validation_step: Verify the plan has a realistic buffer for known and unknown disruptions.
action_map.minimum_test: Block the calendar for the full 26 weeks. Mark known unavailable days (work deadlines, travel, holidays). Recalculate required daily wordcount on the remaining days.
action_map.success_metric: Recalculated daily target ≤500 words AND ≥3 weeks of explicit buffer remain AND fewer than 30 unavailable days.
action_map.failure_threshold: Recalculated target >600 words/day, OR <2 weeks of buffer, OR >40 unavailable days already known.
action_map.next_action: If pass: commit. If fail: extend to 9 months, OR cut wordcount target to 60,000, OR delay the start until a less-disrupted 6-month window.
